label: churn200-s1
summary: The model predicts churn mainly from two usage rules plus a linear score. Heavy daytime use without a voice-mail plan pushes predicted risk towards certainty: switching that part off lowers training AUC from 0.930 to 0.755, and the 101 heavy day users without a plan (threshold in that part's hypothesis) have a mean predicted risk of 83%. Many customer service calls raise risk, more so at a low day charge: the 318 customers with many calls (threshold in that part's hypothesis) have a mean predicted risk of 43%, and switching that part off lowers AUC to 0.838. The direct linear part (international plan up, voice-mail plan down, voice-mail messages up, international minutes up, state offsets) lowers AUC to 0.874 when switched off. The parts add on the logit scale. A long voice-mail chain is inert because its gate is shut on every training row (0 rows open), and a state-and-international-minutes hinge and several single-input state units are small corrections. Coverage is full and the explanation reproduces the model to within 3.3e-16.
